beats.delivery: Professional, concise, and paced for an introductory business audience.
beats.narration: An information system is not just an application. Imagine a customer places an order. A person confirms the request, a process defines what should happen next, data records the facts, and technology moves that record to the people who fulfill and monitor the order. A useful system coordinates all four parts around a business outcome.
beats.title: Connect people, process, data, and technology
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-mis | Move a customer order through a salesperson, a defined fulfillment process, a shared data record, and an information system.

beats.delivery: Professional, concise, and paced for an introductory business audience.
beats.narration: The order becomes useful only when its data is trustworthy. Required fields are validated, identifiers connect related records, and business rules prevent impossible states. The same reliable record can support inventory, billing, customer service, and fulfillment without each team inventing a different version of what happened.
beats.title: Turn an event into trustworthy information
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-mis | Validate the order identifier, customer, items, inventory status, price, and fulfillment state before sharing one trustworthy record with inventory, billing, and fulfillment.

beats.delivery: Professional, concise, and paced for an introductory business audience.
beats.narration: Managers do not need every database row. They need a decision view: are orders late, where do exceptions occur, and which change would improve the outcome? A dashboard summarizes evidence, but people still interpret it in context. Their decision can revise staffing, inventory rules, or the process itself. That feedback loop is the purpose of MIS: use information to improve how the organization works.
beats.title: Convert operational data into a decision
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-mis | Compare promised and actual fulfillment time, stock availability, exception count, and customer outcome on a manager's dashboard, then feed the decision back into the process.

claims.text: Management information systems connect technology, people, and processes to support and improve business operations.
RIT's MIS curriculum includes analyzing business processes and designing practical information systems that use databases and enterprise technologies.
Data visualization and analysis can generate managerial insight, while business-process analysis can guide improved information-system design.

sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.excerpt: RIT describes management information systems as the connection among technology, people, and processes that supports and improves business operations. The program emphasizes analyzing existing business processes, designing usable and cost-effective information systems, working with databases and enterprise systems, and using data visualization and analysis to generate managerial insight. Student teams apply project-management techniques to real business situations while developing information systems.
